messages:
Maya Chen: FYI opened a docs PR with a step-by-step repro for the intermittent 429s we saw in staging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/587
Jordan Patel: nice, sgtm. does the repro need the env var tweak we discussed? (token window and client concurrency)
Maya Chen: yep—added section under 'Troubleshooting -> Rate limits' showing how to reproduce with local loadgen. snippet:
```
# repro: hit with 120 concurrent reqs, client-side window=64
for i in range(120): run_request("/v1/generate", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer $TEST_KEY"})
```
Jordan Patel: can we also include the SDK snippet for backoff? people keep copy/pasting the naive retry.
kevin: I pushed a follow-up commit with the JS SDK example using exponential backoff + jitter. PTAL @Maya
Maya Chen: thanks. can we also add a short paragraph about fallback model behavior? one-page note that 429 -> try fallback model (lower throughput) rather than blindly retrying.
Priya Singh: make sure to mention the 429 header fields we return now: X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After. I can add screenshot of cURL response.
Maya Chen: added both, left a TODO about canarying the change in the dedicated docs (enterprise customers). @Sam can you review for tone/accuracy?
Sam: reviewing now. small nit: in the code block use `await Promise.allSettled(...)` in the example, otherwise people will hammer with naive Promise.all.
Sam: also suggest adding short troubleshooting checklist at the top: reproduce -> check headers -> apply backoff -> consider fallback model -> contact support with request IDs.
Maya Chen: done. I've updated the PR description with checklist and linked the runtime playbook: https://internal.redwood.ai/playbooks/runtime-rate-limits
Jordan Patel: any objections to merging tomorrow after Sam's final pass? we should also add a short note to the changelog.
kevin: lgtm from SDK side. can add code snippet for python later.
Priya Singh: I'll add the cURL screenshot in a follow-up commit.
Maya Chen: merging after Sam OKs. thanks all :tada:
